conventions.name: workspace-package-layout
conventions.description: Every package under packages/ carries the same four files. package.json and tsconfig.json are the build contract; CLAUDE.md is the package guide the root guide links (check:claude-md asserts the link); vitest.config.ts is where the suite is defined once, since the root config discovers suites by glob rather than declaring them.

conventions.name: package-vitest-config
conventions.description: Each package's vitest.config.ts spreads the shared config rather than re-declaring it: writing test:{} without ...sharedConfig.test REPLACES the shared object, which is how every package silently lost `reporters`.

conventions.name: publishable-package-layout
conventions.description: The three published packages additionally carry a README (npm's landing page), a tsconfig.build.json (the declaration emit, and the only program that rejects a cross-package relative import) and a tsdown.config.ts.

conventions.name: barrel-files
conventions.description: A *-barrel.ts file is a pure re-export surface. A local declaration in one is a symbol with no home module, invisible to the follow-the-re-export-chain rule the import conventions rest on.

conventions.name: core-package-boundary
conventions.description: packages/aai is the base of the dependency graph — every other package depends on it and it depends on none of them.

conventions.name: cli-package-boundary
conventions.description: The CLI must never import from the server or the guest. The one edge between them runs the other way (aai-guest imports the CLI's public build-hook subpaths), and it is a hard boundary because the CLI ships to users while the server and guest are private platform code.

conventions.name: guest-package-boundary
conventions.description: The guest never imports server code — that hard boundary is the reason the guest is its own package. aai-server depends on aai-guest only to resolve its built artifact, never to import guest source.

conventions.name: browser-package-boundary
conventions.description: aai-ui is a browser client. It may depend on the core SDK and nothing else in the workspace — a platform or CLI import here would pull server code into a browser bundle.

conventions.name: llm-providers
conventions.description: Every LLM provider module exports the same four-symbol shape. assemblyai.ts is excluded: it is the one vendor with a module per kind, so its symbols carry a kind infix (ASSEMBLYAI_LLM_KIND) the shared template cannot express.

conventions.name: stt-providers
conventions.description: Every STT provider module exports the provider shape plus the resolve*Settings helper the pipeline transport calls to fold a provider's options into its session defaults.

conventions.name: tts-providers
conventions.description: Every TTS provider module exports the STT shape plus a default voice — the one setting a TTS provider cannot infer.

conventions.name: s2s-providers
conventions.description: S2S providers take the same kind/env-var pair as the pipeline providers. Options is a type rather than an interface here, because an S2S provider's options mirror the vendor's own session shape.

conventions.name: agent-templates
conventions.description: Every template is a complete agent project a user can scaffold: agent.ts is its entry, client.tsx (when present) is the browser half, and each tools/ file is one tool.

conventions.name: template-tools
conventions.description: A tools/ file is named for the snake_case tool name the LLM sees (Biome's filename convention is overridden for exactly this reason) and exports one const named for it in camelCase.
